subject: Clarifying retainer, overtime billing & escalation coverage for pilot
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@starlane.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Retainer & escalation: pilot SLO questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Starlane's product team is excited to kick off the 6-week pilot. Before we finalize the statement of work, a couple of quick pricing/SLA clarifications so I can route to procurement: 

1) Retainer vs hourly overtime: for fast-path escalations outside normal business hours, do you bill by an hourly overage or is that folded into a retainer? We need predictable capex signaling for the finance team.

2) Weekend coverage: our core users are in PST/EDT but we have weekend spikes — what does your escalation roster look like on Saturdays/Sundays? Do weekend contacts incur a premium?

3) Surge credits: if Redwood cannot meet the agreed uptime window for the pilot (tier-2), what's the credit calculation? We saw some language in the draft SOW but wanted a worked example (1 hour downtime -> $X credit).

If you can share the current pricing file and a short worked example, I'll attach both to the procurement packet.

Cheers,
Oliver
Head of Ops, Starlane
oliver@starlane.ai

Hi Oliver — quick answers and attached a pricing workbook (SLA_Tier_Pricing_v3.xlsx) with worked examples. Summary below:

1) Retainer vs hourly: We offer two models for pilots — (A) small retainer that covers triage + a fixed number of off-hours escalations per month (recommended for pilots), or (B) pay-as-you-go hourly for any overtime beyond standard coverage. For the 6-week pilot we typically recommend option A to keep procurement sign-off simple. The attached sheet has numeric examples (rows 12-18).

2) Weekend coverage: Weekend roster is available as an add-on. Base response windows apply Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 PT. Weekend coverage (Sat–Sun) is provided by the regional on-call at a 1.5x premium inside a retainer, and 2.0x for pure hourly billables. If you expect predictable weekend traffic, we can include a weekend band in the pilot retainer for a fixed uplift (example in the sheet).

3) Surge credits: We calculate credits on a per-incident basis using the formula in the draft SOW: credit = (downtime minutes / monthly SLO minutes) * monthly retainer. For pilots we can offer a simple slab: <30m = 0.25x daily pro-rata, 30–240m = 1x daily pro-rata, >240m = 3x daily pro-rata. Worked examples in the attachment (sheet: Credits).

Action items: 
- I'll attach a sample escalation roster CSV for your team to review (escalation_roster_sample.csv).
- Priyom — can you confirm whether we want to propose a pilot retainer with a 3-call off-hours allowance before hourly billing?
- Karthik — please confirm the weekend multiplier we want to standardize for pilots (1.5x ok?).

Oliver — if the numbers look ok, I can produce a short addendum to the SOW that spells out the pilot retainer and the weekend add-on.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Thanks Hannah — the attachment looks helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement/ops: 

- Weekend premium: 1.5x inside a retainer is reasonable, but procurement is asking whether that uplift is billed pro-rata if only one weekend day is requested in the month. Example: we have a one-off launch pushed to a Sunday — will we be charged the full weekend band, or can we pay a one-day pro-rata?

- Off-hours allowances: your 3-call allowance sounds fair. Are calls defined as incidents (i.e., one ticket) or discrete phone escalations? We have a high fanout during incidents and prefer incident-based counting.

- Credit look: the slab approach is OK but could be a show-stopper for finance. Can Redwood provide an explicit $/hour example tied to our projected retainer so the CFO can see the worst case balance? For our pilot retainer of $18,000/month (example), what would 1hr / 4hr / 8hr downtime equate to in dollars under your slab?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — if you can send a one-page worked example with numbers, procurement should be able to wrap this week.

Best,
Oliver

Oliver — thanks, I've put together the one-page worked example below and attached the escalation roster sample. Priyom/Laura/Karthik, tagging you for internal confirmation on operational notes.

Worked example (pilot retainer = $18,000/month):
- Monthly SLO minutes (30d): 43,200 minutes
- Slab credit formula (as discussed): <30m = 0.25x daily pro-rata, 30–240m = 1x daily pro-rata, >240m = 3x daily pro-rata.

Calculate daily pro-rata = monthly retainer / 30 = $600/day.
- 1 hour downtime (60m) falls in 30–240m slab -> credit = 1x daily pro-rata = $600
- 4 hours downtime (240m) -> still 30–240m -> credit = $600
- 8 hours downtime (480m) -> >240m -> credit = 3x daily pro-rata = $1,800

Notes on your questions: 
- Weekend pro-rata: yes — we can offer a one-day pro-rata for a single weekend day request (we'll bill the weekend day as daily pro-rata of the weekend band). If you only need a single Sunday launch we won't require you to purchase the full month weekend band. We'll add that as a clause in the addendum.
- Incident counting: incidents are defined by ticket ID in our tracking system (PagerDuty/Jira). Multiple phone calls related to the same ticket count as one incident. If you prefer call-based billing, we can do that, but it will be a separate line item.

Operational ask for Redwood internal team: 
- Priyom: confirm we push the incident definition into the SOW (ticket-based).
- Karthik: approve weekend multiplier for pilots at 1.5x inside a retainer.
- Laura: once approved, can you draft the short addendum that includes the pro-rata weekend clause and the three-call allowance details? We'll keep the SOW language tight so procurement can sign.

Oliver — if that looks good I will send the SOW addendum (one page) and a redline to your counsel.

Thanks,
